input.strategy_title: Bundle an S3-compatible object store for disconnected installs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Pipelines and model serving both require S3-compatible object storage, but
disconnected customers frequently have none. Field teams work around this by
installing upstream MinIO ad hoc — unsupported, unpatched, and invisible to the
platform. We want a supported, bundled S3-compatible store that administrators
can enable for disconnected and PoC clusters. The leading candidate, MinIO, is
AGPL-3.0 licensed; redistribution terms must be cleared before any productization
work can ship, and the outcome may force a different upstream.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Legal review of redistributing the candidate object store (MinIO, AGPL-3.0) is completed and documented, including the derivative-work posture for operator integration. This clearance blocks all shipping work. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible object store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and upgrade lifecycle. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Data Science Pipelines and model serving connection defaults can target the bundled store without manual endpoint configuration. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers enablement, sizing guidance, and the supported/unsupported boundary versus customer-provided storage. |

## Affected Components

- Platform Operator
- Data Science Pipelines
- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Replacing customer-provided S3 in connected environments
- Data migration tooling between stores

## Open Questions

1. If AGPL terms cannot be satisfied for our distribution model, the fallback
   candidate is an Apache-2.0 alternative (e.g. SeaweedFS) — acceptable, but it
   restarts image productization.

## Description

Creates the midstream repository for MinIO under opendatahub-io so a
productized, supported store image can be built from source. Executed only if
the legal clearance grants AGPL-3.0 redistribution for MinIO; if clearance is
denied, the Apache-2.0 fallback branch replaces this work.

- Create the midstream repository for MinIO under opendatahub-io, mirroring the
  selected upstream version.
- Establish branching and versioning conventions consistent with other midstream
  components.

- A midstream repository for MinIO exists under opendatahub-io, mirroring the
  selected upstream version.
- The repository follows the organization's conventions for midstream components.

# Productize the MinIO image with upgrade lifecycle

## Description

Productizes MinIO as the supported bundled store image: platform image-hardening
standards, a version/upgrade policy, and a published pinned digest for the
Platform Operator's enablement configuration. Runs after the midstream repository
exists and license validation passes, in parallel with the Konflux onboarding.

## Scope

- Productized MinIO container image meeting platform image-hardening standards.
- Version and upgrade policy: new upstream versions flow into the midstream
  repository and through the build pipeline without manual rebuild
  orchestration.
- Publish the pinned image digest for consumption by the Platform Operator
  enablement packaging (a configuration reference filled in at execution time).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The productized MinIO image is published and meets platform image standards.
- An upgrade to a new store image version builds and ships through the pipeline
  without manual rebuild orchestration.
- The build pipeline is green for the image (gates this epic's completion even
  though pipeline onboarding runs in parallel).
- The pinned digest of the productized image is available for the operator's
  enablement configuration.

## HLR Traceability

# Midstream repo onboarding for the Apache-2.0 fallback object store

## Description

Creates the midstream repository for the Apache-2.0 licensed fallback object
store under opendatahub-io so a productized, supported store image can be built
from source. Executed only if the legal clearance denies AGPL-3.0 redistribution
for MinIO; per the strategy's open question, this restarts image productization
with the fallback upstream. The clearance decision names the specific fallback
upstream to productize; this epic validates that named candidate's S3
compatibility and onboards it. If MinIO is cleared instead, the MinIO branch
replaces this work.

## Scope

- Validate the S3 compatibility of the fallback upstream named by the legal
  clearance decision against the platform's needs (the Pipelines and model
  serving S3 workloads), and document the validation results. Escalate any gap
  that would disqualify the named candidate back to the clearance decision
  rather than substituting a different upstream here.
- Create the midstream repository for the named fallback store under
  opendatahub-io, mirroring the selected upstream version.
- Establish branching and versioning conventions consistent with other midstream
  components.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The S3 compatibility of the named fallback upstream is validated against
  platform needs and documented, with any disqualifying gap escalated back to
  the clearance decision.
- A midstream repository for the named fallback store exists under
  opendatahub-io, mirroring the selected upstream version.
- The repository follows the organization's conventions for midstream components.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): enabling — productized, supported images require a midstream
  source repository.

| adapter_pattern | 0 | No reference implementation prescribed; standard scanning tooling. |
| existing_foundation | +1 | Established license-scanning tooling and reporting conventions exist. |
| open_questions | +1 | The Apache-2.0 posture is comparatively low-risk, and the legal-clearance decision names the specific fallback upstream before this branch starts, so the scan target is fixed when this epic begins. |
| external_dependency | 0 | No upstream contribution or vendor coordination needed to run scans. |
| human_process_gates | -1 | Findings on conflicting licenses require escalation to legal for resolution. |

# Platform Operator enablement of the bundled S3-compatible object store

## Description

Delivers the administrator-facing enablement of a supported, bundled S3-compatible
object store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and a managed
upgrade lifecycle, targeting disconnected and PoC clusters where no
customer-provided object storage exists. This epic is upstream-agnostic: it
enablements whichever store the legal clearance selects, and consumes the
productized store image as a configuration reference (pinned digest) rather than
building against it.

## Scope

- Add an enablement path in the Platform Operator so administrators can turn the
  bundled S3-compatible store on through operator configuration, with no external
  network access required (disconnected installs).
- Deploy and manage the store using the productized store image, referenced by
  pinned digest; the digest is filled in at execution time once the productized
  image is published.
- Manage the upgrade lifecycle: platform upgrades must not orphan or break an
  enabled bundled store.
- Provide a disable/rollback path so administrators can turn the bundled store off
  and fall back to customer-provided storage configuration — the supported
  replacement for the ad-hoc, unsupported upstream MinIO installs field teams
  perform today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a disconnected cluster, an administrator can enable the bundled S3-compatible
  store through Platform Operator configuration with no external network access.
- The enabled store runs the productized image referenced by a pinned digest, and
  that digest is available at execution time.
- A platform upgrade on a cluster with the bundled store enabled completes without
  breaking the store or requiring manual reconfiguration.
- Administrators can disable the bundled store, with components falling back to
  customer-provided storage configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible object
  store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and upgrade
  lifecycle.
